title: Arbitrary-field control of complementary-open module direct images
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $N\ge1$ be invertible in $k$ with $NA=0$. Let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and let $j:W\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open $k$-immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites and their higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. There exists $d\ge0$ such that every field extension $L/k$ satisfies $\dim(W_L)\le d$ [def-kun-dimension, def-pc-fibre-product]. For any such $d$, the following assertions hold with the same constant $c=2d$:
$$R^qj_*M=0\qquad(q>c)$$
for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$, with no constructibility hypothesis on $M$; and $R^qj_*F$ is constructible for every constructible $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every integer $q$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Equivalently, $(W,T)$ satisfies the ordinary-etale open-complement condition at $A$ with $c=2d$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound]. No separable-closedness or finite absolute cohomological-dimension hypothesis is imposed on $k$. Empty $W$ and $T$ are allowed.

proof.text: Write $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_W=a_Tj$. The quasi-compact open immersion $j$ is of finite type by lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type. Composition with $a_T$ is of finite type by lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change (1), so $W$ is of finite type over $k$. Apply lem-kun-uniform-field-extension-dimension-bound to $a_W$ to obtain a natural $d$ bounding every $W_L$. Its statement allows empty schemes. Now fix any natural $d$ with the bound in the item, rather than only the particular bound just obtained.

source.place: Closed-immersion paragraph: complementary-open input; geometry and uniform bound. Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type) and 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); BaseChangeDimension.lean, exists_topologicalKrullDim_le_of_isPullback.

proof.text: Let $M$ be any $A$-module sheaf on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and let $U_WM$ be its underlying abelian sheaf. Every local section $m$ satisfies $Nm=(N1_A)m=0$, so $U_WM$ is torsion. Apply lem-kun-torsion-abelian-direct-image-dimension-bound to $a_W,a_T,j$, with $a_Tj=a_W$ and the chosen field-extension bound: $R^qj_*(U_WM)=0$ for every $q>2d$. By lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison this sheaf is isomorphic to $U_T(R^qj_*M)$. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero: on every object its underlying group has only the zero element. Thus $R^qj_*M=0$. No constructibility of $M$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd (1), in the quantitative arbitrary-field refinement recorded by lem-kun-torsion-abelian-direct-image-dimension-bound; coefficient comparison: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, and 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: For a constructible $A$-module sheaf $F$, the complex $F[0]$ is bounded constructible: its only possibly nonzero cohomology is $F$ in degree zero. Apply thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility to $j:W\to T$. Both schemes are of finite type over the same field by Step 1; $A$ is finite, $NA=0$, and $N$ is invertible in $k$, exactly the coefficient hypotheses of that theorem. Hence $Rj_*F[0]$ is bounded constructible. By the definitions, each $R^qj_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rj_*F[0])$ is constructible, for every integer $q$.

source.place: Theorem statement, applied to a sheaf in degree zero; closed-immersion input of the current blueprint.

proof.text: Take $c=2d\ge0$. Steps 2 and 3 are respectively the two clauses of def-exc-open-complement-bound, so they give the asserted condition with this same $c$. No hypothesis on the absolute cohomological dimension or separable closedness of $k$ entered either step. If $W$ is empty, the dimension-bound lemma still supplies a bound and its sheaf category has only the zero object; both conclusions hold. Empty $T$ forces empty $W$, so that case is covered too.

The delivery has no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Step 1: the quasi-compact open-immersion node gives that j is of finite type, and finite-type composition (1) gives the same for W. lem-kun-uniform-field-extension-dimension-bound needs locally of finite type plus quasi-compact over a field; it gives the existence of d for every field base change, empty schemes allowed. The step then fixes an arbitrary admissible d, as the item requires. Step 2: I checked the torsion-abelian vanishing hypotheses against its Lean statement at TorsionAbelianDirectImageVanishing.lean:204 (no sorry): finite-type aW and aT, aT j = aW, the field-base-change bound, and torsion via N·1_A = 0. The result is moved to A-modules with lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison, which holds in every degree for any Lambda, plus zero reflection, which is elementary. No cd(k) or constructibility assumption is used. Step 3: thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility has exactly the item's hypotheses (finite A killed by an N invertible in k, finite type over a field, no separatedness). Together with the D^b_c definition and R^q = H^q(Rj_*F[0]), it gives constructibility in every degree. Step 4: the two clauses of def-exc-open-complement-bound are exactly Steps 2 and 3 with c = 2d. Stacks tags 01T5, 01T3, 03FD, 072W and 0F10 are all correct in tags/tags. Tag 0F10 gives only finiteness, and the quantitative 2d comes from the existing node, as the report says. Edge cases checked: W or T empty, d = 0, j = id, N = 1 forcing A = 0, and k = R with W = G_m in A^1 (stalk of cd at most 1). No duplicate: thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional (k separably closed) and lem-exc-open-complement-known (k = F̄_q) are strictly narrower. The tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch 5: the cited torsion-abelian node reaches only def-trf-schematically-dense-open, a general definition. Relative finite cohomological dimension is neither assumed by nor a step of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, so the citation is allowed. No SGA source is used.
